The British sealed the underground portions and what remains above is just a pale shadow of the old grand palace.

title: File:JOYSAGAR TANK.jpg
author: Hiranmoy Boruah
description: JOYSAGAR TANK,SIVASAGAR, Largest of all the tanks built by Ahom Kings in Assam. It is considered as the largest men made pond in India. The water level of the tanks stays at 14 feet higher than ground level. The Tank Jayasagar was dug by Ahom king Rudrasingha (1696-1714) to commemorate his mother Sati Joymoti, wife of Gadapani, later King Gadadharsingha (1681-1695). The place was chosen, where Siulikpha convicted Joyamoti through his Chaodangs to extract information regarding her exiled husband Gadapani. This is the biggest man-made tank comprising an area of 318 acres including the four banks.

title: File:Charaideo Maidam.jpg
author: Aliahmed2021
description:
Maidam - tumuli of the Ahom Kingdom
A unique creation of the Ahom Dynasty of Assam ruling the Ahom Kingdom through 1228 AD to 1826 AD. They buried their kings and members of the royal family in a burrow shaped mound of earth with structures of bricks all around it. The monument resembled the Egyptian pyramids with only the difference of the raw materials used. Hundreds of such maidams are still found scattered all around Assam's Sivasagar district, Dibrugarh, Jorhat and Golaghat districts glorifying the rich cultural traditions of the Ahoms. The Charaideo maidam area is preserved by the ASI as well as by the State Government's agency in two parts as a place of historical importance and it is open for public viewing on weekdays.

title: File:Sibasagar Shiva Doul 04.jpg
author: Nayan j Nath
description:
Shiva Dol is a historic 18th-century temple complex in Sivasagar, Assam, comprising Sivadol (dedicated to Lord Shiva), Vishnudol (to Lord Vishnu), and Devidol (to Goddess Durga), along with a museum. Built in 1734 by Queen Bar Raja Ambika during the reign of Ahom king Swargadeo Siva Singha, the temples stand on the banks of the grand Sivasagar Tank (Borpukhuri). The Sivadol, towering at 104 feet and crowned with a golden dome, is the tallest and most prominent, symbolizing the architectural grandeur of the Ahom dynasty.  .mw-parser-output
